content.title: Dissemination workshop on domestic violence
content.summary: A Workshop on Domestic Violence was organised by the Department of Community Health Sciences (CHS) of the Aga Khan University on November 21, 2000, to disseminate the results of a WHO funded study on the subject in Karachi.

content.text: A Workshop on Domestic Violence was organised by the Department of Community Health Sciences (CHS) of the Aga Khan University on November 21, 2000, to disseminate the results of a WHO funded study on the subject in Karachi. This study was conducted in 1998-99 in middle and 10w- income communities, amongst all Pakistani ethnic groups living in Karachi.

The objective of the Workshop was to highlight the issue of violence in the home. Results of the testimonies of 108 victims were presented. Violence and abuse is a multidimensional problem, involving women and men, societal norms and practices. Husbands along with the in-laws were the main perpetrators (in over 90 per cent of cases), as well as fathers, brothers and sisters. Evidence was found for a whole spectrum of violence from verbal to severe physical, economic, psychological and sexual abuse. Stereotypical roles in which women are seen as subordinate to men, economic issues and access to legal rights, constrain a woman's ability to exercise choices that would enable her to end abuse. Of the 31 women who reported severe physical abuse, 18 did not initiate legal action.

Some 60 community members, including both women and men, from squatter settlements where CHS has or had Primary Health Programmes, participated. There were representatives from Orangi, Chanesar Goth, Grax, Essa Nagri, Azam Basti, Ibrahim Hyderi, Rehri Goth, Hijrat Colony and Sultanabad. Dr Fauziah Rabbani, Assistant Professor, CHS, and members of the research team, Ms Zia Sultana and Aneela Zaheer, presented the study's results. This was followed by a lively and very active discussion by the community participants. They identified strategies at the individual, family, community and state levels to creatively deal with the issue of domestic violence with a view to positive change.

The theater group from "Rasti" (the Research and Social Training Institute) under the guidance of Mr. Francis Rufi also performed a skit on domestic violence. The president of one of the field site management teams, Haji Sultan, participated in the skit.

Earlier, Dr Franklin White, Professor and Chairman, CHS, and Dr Asma Fozia Qureshi, Professor, CHS, welcomed the participants. Dr White emphasised that "We must do what we can to lift ourselves out of this culture of violence, and replace it with a culture of mediation that is based on respect for basic human rights, including freedom from fear, especially in one's home. How we value women and children is more than a matter of health priorities. It is a matter of social values and political will."

Ms Fatima Surraiya Bajiya gave the concluding remarks. She emphasised that violence in any form should not be accepted by society. She said that it is important to appreciate that woman and men are both responsible for their actions, that we need to break out of traditional roles and follow the true tenets of Islam.
